doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Piano duos, Mingus and the seventies
title: The 'Spirits' album with Sal Mosca and Ron Carter
summary: They discuss the duo with metronome, and the quartet with Ron Carter and Mousie Alexander.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah and it worked well. Next is a record I find fascinating. The Spirits album with Sal Mosca which is half duo with Sal and then half quartet with Ron Carter and Mousie Alexander which is all basically Tristano-style material either Tristano tunes or a couple of yours.
The duo. I think we each had earphones with a metronome ticking.
Oh really?

Yeah, and that disturbed Dick Katz and Orrin Keepnews a little bit but they didn’t speak up about it. Because [when] left to our own devices, smoking and playing a duo medium tempo ended up being a ballad, et cetera.
That’s like playing with a click track in a way.
Yeah. The music sounds a little . . . I haven’t heard that for years.
I just played it again after not hearing it for years and I thought it’s a great record.
I’d be curious to hear that again because it felt very interesting.
There are four tunes with Ron Carter and Mousie that sound really good. Who’s idea was it to get them on there? It’s a curious choice for a bass player and drummer for a Tristano-type record.
Probably Dick Katz and Orrin. We played at the Village Gate once with Ron and a drummer named Brown. [I] forget his first name.
Sonny Brown?

Sonny Brown; and Sal Mosca, did I say? I think Ron was calling Sal Mosca “The Shadow” or something like that. It didn’t work out at all. Brown came late to the gig and I fired him and he brought me to the union and I didn’t even bother showing up so they fined me and things like that. It was very unpleasant.
You said Ron was reading a newspaper on the date or something, you said earlier?
At the recording session yeah. Very business like.
[Laughing] Okay.
It’s weird.
Is that the only thing you ever did with Ron recording-wise?
I think so.
Mousie I knew. I played in Mousie’s big band that he had for a year or two about thirty years ago.
Yeah. I don’t remember him.
Then he had a stroke and moved to Florida and died a few years later. He was a nice man.
Yeah. Very nice and a nice drummer.
